lesson.menu_desc: Asking, interrupting and joining the conversation politely on an international call -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- Taking the Floor
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Juliana dos Santos Morais | Lesson 3 -- Taking the Floor
lesson.grammar_point: polite requests and permission: can, could, would, may, would you mind + -ing

listenings.text: I facilitate a lot of international meetings, and I see the same problem every week. People who speak English as a second language wait for the perfect moment to speak. They wait for a silence. But in a fast discussion, the perfect moment never comes. So my advice is simple. Use a short phrase to open the door. Could I just add something? Can I chip in here? These phrases give you two or three seconds, and the others stop to listen. Online, you can also raise your hand. It is a good idea. The person who runs the call sees it and gives you the floor. Then you only need your first sentence.

Some years ago, I had a problem. When I did not understand something in a meeting, I did not ask. I thought it was not professional to ask people to repeat. So I just said yes, yes, and I continued. Then one day I sent a proposal to a Canadian partner with the wrong date, because I did not catch it in the call. That was very embarrassing. Now I always ask. I say: sorry, I did not catch that. Would you mind repeating it? Or: could you clarify the second point? And you know what? Nobody thinks it is unprofessional. People think you are careful.

Welcome to the monthly call of our business network. Before we start, here are three simple rules. First, when you are not speaking, please stay on mute. It helps everybody hear better. Second, if you want to speak, raise your hand or write in the chat, and the host will give you the floor. We take turns, so everybody has a chance. And third, please ask if you do not understand something. Many of our members speak English as a second language, so asking someone to repeat or to clarify is always welcome. Thank you, and enjoy the call.
